Standalone feature · Money in intimate relationships

How do I stop being tricked out of money?

This page is not about data. It is about concrete situations: the money has already been asked for and you have not decided whether to give it; or you have given many times, something feels off, and you cannot say exactly what.

Three situations to recognise Two ways to cut your losses Evidence details you can actually use

Contents

  1. Asking for money or a loan soon after meeting
  2. In the name of love — hidden extraction
  3. When you feel wronged and something is off, but cannot name it
  4. If you are being deceived right now, how to stop the loss in time
  5. What was I thinking when I paid?
01

Asking for money or a loan soon after meeting

If you have just met a woman, online or offline, and she asks you for money, a loan or a red envelope —In this situation, the answer is always no.

Most of the time you will notice something is wrong quickly. If someone you have just met asks for a large sum, you will not give it as long as you are not a fool.

But what many people fail to recognise is the following kind: the conversation has gone well and made you feelthere is a chance. Then she asks to borrow a small amount — two or three hundred, five or six hundred — and promises to pay it back soon.

If I do not lend it, will she think I am stingy and turn cold?

If I do lend it, I worry she means no good and will never pay it back.

At that point people often gamble: lend it, she promised to repay, the amount is within what I can afford, we are getting along, so she is probably a decent person.

This choice usually ends with losing both the money and the person. Some fare worse: loan after loan, never even meeting her, and no way to get the money back.

Stop and ask one question

Why would you refuse without hesitation if someone you had just met asked to borrow 100,000, yet start wavering over 200, or a 200-yuan red envelope?

Because you want to spend a little money to buy her continued warmth, continued conversation, continued emotional attention. You fear that if you do not lend it, she will go cold and stop replying.

In fact, at that moment you are secretly hijacked by the inner judgement that"only money makes a woman attracted to you", without noticing it. Precisely because that judgement is there, you worry she will think you are stingy, and you waver.

Besides wanting to buy emotional attention with money, there is also theavailability principle: once you start investing emotionally, feel there is a chance, and feel she is attainable, you begin to be led by her behaviour — and that is when reality is hardest to see.

Anything that can make you sway, waver or hesitate must have been preceded by some emotional value she gave you, enough to make you feel — maybe there is a chance.

But look at this:She is warm only around the times you give her money; whenever no money is involved, that warmth disappears.Then there is a problem.

Observing your own mind

Once you see the emotion, it can no longer hijack you

Ah, I am wavering over whether to lend it. Reason says no, but a very strong emotion is hijacking me and telling me: if I do not lend it, she will go cold. I am afraid of that, and I want her to keep being warm.

See that emotion, see your fear and your longing, see your most honest feeling — once you see it, it cannot hijack you, and then you can make the right decision, and may even see the real reason she is asking to borrow money.

Understand this: whether a woman likes you has no necessary connection to money. Without money, good looks or height, she can still like you and fall in love with you. Yet some people still believe deep down that only money can attract women.

It is fine if you cannot drop that judgement for now, but build yourself asafety rail— to keep that judgement from letting someone trick you out of money. Because that belief sits at the bottom, people often pay women money they never should have.

Try swapping roles: if you had known someone for only a week or two, would you ask them for a loan? Do you think they would lend it? Under what conditions would you be certain they would give it to you?

02

In the name of love — hidden extraction

The first kind — asking for money outright — is fairly easy to spot; the method is not subtle and the other side has invested little emotional value.

Hidden extraction, by contrast, often comes wrapped in "in the name of love", making youwillinglypay. It is harder to detect because the other side really has invested considerable emotional value — or at least made you feel she has. This usually happens in two phases: while courting, and after the relationship is confirmed.

1) The courting phase

If every meal out is suggested by her, at a restaurant she chooses, with dishes she likes, and she never pays a cent or once says "next time is on me" —you can basically be sure this is hidden extraction.

What you can see is that she cares more about going to that restaurant than about the date with you — she just needs someone to pay.

Do you still want to continue? If so, the next time she suggests a meal, can you say the words to her directly —

"Sure, but you are paying this time."

Or you can propose a different restaurant, or tea instead. Use being short on time or switching to coffee at another hour as the reason, and put the focus on your conversation rather than the meal.

2) After the relationship is confirmed

Another case: you are already a couple, but she has never introduced you to her friends, family or anyone close, and has never made the relationship public. In other words she never lets you into her life — even as boyfriend and girlfriend, even after becoming intimate, you still know nothing about her life or her past. (This criterion applies to women too.)

On top of that she often asks you to buy bags, designer goods, phones and watches, or to transfer money and send red envelopes, while never giving anything back. If you refuse, you do not love her; she goes cold and argues until you give in.

At that point, an alarm should go off in your mind:Does she really love you, or does she have another purpose?

If you are sure there is no problem and do not feel tired or bitter — even eating instant noodles every day to save money for expensive gifts and transfers — you will be dumped once you can no longer afford it. Is a whole lifetime of that worth it?

Transference

Treat a woman like your mother and you will "willingly be deceived"

Many people are starved of love. They roughly know what a normal relationship looks like, but because they are so deprived and so desperate to hold on to this small warmth, they let themselves be hijacked even when treated badly. Reason says no, but the emotional brain does not obey reason; they give and are deceived willingly.

If an infant's needs are not met by the mother, it grows anxious that "mother does not love me unconditionally", and death anxiety arises. An infant is fragile and can only survive with careful care; a lack of love, attention or care immediately triggers death anxiety. That care lies in the mother's hands, so the moment her mood shifts the infant becomes extremely anxious — its survival depends on her, and her mood cannot be controlled. What do you do to make life easier? — satisfy "mother's" demands.

Grow up, and once transference happens in a relationship — treating a woman as your mother — you will meet her demands unconditionally and end up "willingly deceived". Because as an infant there was no other choice,but you are no longer an infant, and she is not your mother.

Being dumped or abandoned then brings death anxiety. The energy of that emotion is enormous; it can hijack a person and make them feel unbearable pain — most people who have been through a breakup know it. If it rises and you do not see it, it can briefly outweigh even the fear of real death and drive you to do something you will regret.

So remember:Every suffering passes.The emotion that is tearing you apart right now will pass too.

Everything passes.Do not act on impulse; do not do something you cannot take back.

If by then none of the above helps and the pain is still unbearable, if you feel about to do something foolish on impulse, remember this line:

The vast world holds nothing to cling to. Come and go as you will, free and unbound. If life is to be lived, live it — do not seek a substitute.

Watch the emotion rise, peak and fade; do nothing, just see it. That is why the regular exercises in Instant Confidence matter — building inner strength lets you catch the whole arc from rising to vanishing before it hijacks you.

When it comes to spending money on a woman, you will then naturally know what is worth paying for and what is not worth a cent. Sometimesnot spending money is what makes respect for you rise in her heart; send her money and she loses that respect deep down, because she knows she can shake you and hijack you — as a woman, she will feel you cannot be relied on.

03

When you feel wronged and something is off, but cannot name it

Many people have this worry in a relationship: whether going out or having dinner, the other person never pays a cent; even after getting together, you cover all living costs. It feels unfair and stifling, and you ask yourself: am I being stingy, or am I being drained?

It depends on the situation.

If you are not yet a couple, and this is not the case in item 02 where she suggests the meal, picks the restaurant, orders what she likes and pays nothing, but ratheryou did the inviting— then you cannot label her a gold digger. In some cases a man being gentlemanly and picking up the bill is nothing to make a fuss about.

Since you invited her, could you not choose a restaurant that fits your finances and order within your budget, instead of leaving every decision to her and then feeling bad when the bill exceeds what you expected — and pinning a label on her for it? That would be biting the hand that fed you.

If you are already a couple and the behaviour in item 02 has been ruled out, then this is not really a question of extraction at all, but of:How should money be spent in a relationship?

Inner strength

Do not put yourself down first

If the current way of spending already makes you uncomfortable, do not start by putting yourself down or calling yourself stingy. Suppressing it will cause trouble, and the emotion will eventually erupt. It is your real feeling right now; you are afraid to show it, and you are even denying your own reaction.

This is a shortage of inner strength. What does that mean? It means we do not dare to act on what we genuinely feel. And that "not daring" is really a lack of trust in our own honest feeling.

So the first step is building inner strength. Once there is enough of it, the spotlight turns naturally onto the other person and you truly see what kind of person she is; you also see how far you are willing to give of your own accord, rather than out of fear that she will think you stingy, abandon you or leave.

04

If you are being deceived right now, how to stop the loss in time

  1. Stop outrightThis is the most direct and most useful action. Many people cannot manage it because that emotion hijacks them unseen, and they end up giving more and more.
  2. Use the law to protect your interestsBelow are steps you can follow down to every detail; see the box.

①Write "loan" in the transfer note

When lending money by transfer, note it as a loan. Then, whether or not a written IOU exists, the relationship is clearly a loan. If it is not repaid later, whether a few hundred or tens of thousands, you can file suit to recover it.

②If you hesitate to write "loan", note the person's real name instead

Worried that a direct "loan" note will offend them? Another approach works too: write their real name in the transfer note; it carries the same legal weight.

③Large transfers ask for a real name — ask for it early

Large transfers prompt you to enter the recipient's real name. Ask for the name right at the start — then, if a transfer really becomes necessary, you can double-check that the name given to you is genuine.

So if someone you have just met asks to borrow money and will not even tell you their name, is that not a problem?

④Best not to hand over cash

Even with a written IOU, the other side may deny that any loan took place. A lawsuit then takes a long time and requires a lot of evidence. Bank transfers with a note are the better route.

⑤If they ask you to note "voluntary gift", take it as a warning

If a woman actively asks you to write "voluntary gift" in the transfer note, that is a warning sign.

⑥No note, and they have disappeared

If the transfer had no note identifying it as a loan, and now you want the money back but the person has vanished: where the amount exceeds 3,000 yuan and fraud is involved, a case can be filed for recovery.

⑦Transfers with special numbers cannot be recovered

The Civil Code treats transfers containing special numeric meanings during a relationship — such as 520 or 1314 — as gifts, so they cannot be recovered.

05

What was I thinking when I paid?

Which brings us back to the one core question:What was I thinking when I paid?

Nothing at all.What occupied my mind instead was what she seemed to like eating, where to go next time, where to take her afterwards. To me her smile was the best return.

Not that it was blind spending: nothing beyond my means, because we are both adults, andtwo people who respect and value themselves will not put the other in an awkward position.

Remember: money cannot buy genuine feelings.

A final reminder

Do not label people right away, but be honest with yourself

Once "observing your own mind" brings you to a certain level of the "momentary true self", you will find that even a woman who originally intended to extract money will, on meeting you, be won over and give it up entirely — wanting instead more love and attention from you. Because once you are truly loved, you discover that love is worth far more than money. At that point, all the more so for other women.

It is only while we are still starved of love and do not yet know how to give it that we tend to attract people who extract money in love's name.

But nor should we label people from the outset. Once we reach that breadth and height, the very category of "gold digger" no longer exists in our eyes.

But take care!Be honest about where you actually are inside. Do not, while still short of that level, let "wanting" hijack you into believing you have arrived, then get involved with people you should not and end up paying for it.

So until you truly awaken to that self and reach that state, you still need the precautions above to protect yourself.

If the answer is no money, then no money.
If the answer is not to get involved, then do not get involved.
Next · Rules of action

Push back on exploitation, and on shrinking back

The judgements above compressed into seven rules you can act on: assume the risk exists, leave the moment one-sided giving appears within a year, do not show how much you need it, and put loving yourself first.
